stories.head: Klaviyo acquires AI startup Agency, names founder Elias Torres Chief Product Officer
stories.plain: Klaviyo is buying Agency, an AI-native customer success firm, and putting its co-founder in charge of product. This is a significant strategic acquisition that shapes how one of the biggest B2C CRM platforms will build and sell AI features going forward — directly affecting how marketers buy and use autonomous engagement tools.

stories.head: Time magazine serves ads directly to AI crawlers, testing AI-only ad strategy
stories.plain: Time is placing ads inside its pages specifically for AI crawlers — not human readers. If this works, it rewrites how brands spend to stay visible inside AI-generated answers. It is one of the first real-world tests of a paid GEO strategy, making it essential reading for anyone thinking about future media buying.

stories.head: Bloomreach launches multi-agent 'Ask Me Anything' shopping search powered by Loomi
stories.plain: Bloomreach is turning the standard e-commerce search bar into a multi-agent conversational interface that handles keyword search, product questions, and customer service in one place. This is a concrete example of agentic AI reshaping how personalization is delivered on retail sites — and how platforms are being rebuilt around agent architectures.

stories.head: Coca-Cola FEMSA CDO on building one version of data truth across 15 countries and selling governance to the board
stories.plain: Coca-Cola FEMSA's Global CDO explains how a major multinational unified messy data across 15 markets and made the case for data governance at board level. This is a rare, senior practitioner account of the organisational and political work behind AI readiness — directly relevant to anyone building or buying marketing AI infrastructure.

stories.head: Agencies shift from content production to expertise as AI commoditises routine creative work
stories.plain: New research shows agencies are restructuring their business model because AI is making routine content creation nearly worthless. They are pivoting to strategy, judgment, and expertise. This matters for marketers deciding what to keep in-house, what to buy from agencies, and where AI tools replace versus augment human work.

stories.head: Klaviyo acquires AI startup Agency, names co-founder Elias Torres as Chief Product Officer
stories.plain: Klaviyo is buying Agency, an AI-native customer-success company, and putting its CEO in charge of product. This is a direct signal that B2C CRM platforms are racing to embed agentic AI at the core — not bolt it on — changing what buyers should expect from marketing automation vendors and how those platforms get built.

stories.head: Time magazine serves ads directly to AI crawlers, testing a new GEO ad format
stories.plain: Time is experimenting with ads formatted specifically for AI crawlers rather than human readers — a strategy that could let brands buy their way into AI-generated answers. If it scales, it rewrites the rules of paid media and search budgeting, making generative engine optimization a commercial channel, not just an organic tactic.

stories.head: OpenAI ad experiment launches brand-specific AI agents that answer questions and capture leads after the click
stories.plain: OpenAI is testing ads that, when clicked, spin up a dedicated AI agent for that advertiser — answering product questions, recommending items, and collecting leads inside ChatGPT. This collapses the funnel into a single conversational session and forces marketers to think about agentic post-click experiences, not just creative.

stories.head: Bloomreach launches multi-agent 'Ask Me Anything' search powered by its Loomi agentic personalization platform
stories.plain: Bloomreach has turned the standard e-commerce search bar into an agentic, conversational entry point that handles keyword search, natural-language shopping questions, and customer service in one place. It shows how personalization platforms are moving from recommendation engines to multi-agent orchestration — a significant shift in how commerce AI is built and bought.

stories.head: Optimizing your B2B brand for autonomous AI shoppers: when agents do the buying research
stories.plain: As B2B buyers delegate vendor research to AI agents, traditional SEO stops working and brand citation inside AI answers becomes the new battleground. This piece gives marketers a practical framework for ensuring their brand surfaces in agent-driven research — directly relevant to anyone planning content or brand strategy for 2026 budgets.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Eating the Funnel
body: Autonomous AI agents are now acting as buyers, researchers, and decision-makers — not just assistants. Bloomreach's multi-agent search bar, OpenAI's post-click ad experiment, and B2B guidance on optimizing for "autonomous AI shoppers" all point to the same shift: the funnel is being traversed by software, not humans.

This forces a fundamental rethink of who — or what — you are marketing to. Brands that optimize only for human attention are structurally invisible to AI-mediated purchase journeys. The new imperative is making your brand legible to agents as well as people.

themes.head: AI-Only Advertising Opens a New Channel
body: Time magazine's AI-only ad format and Brandtech Jellyfish's "Share of Model" optimisation tool both signal that a distinct AI-native ad channel is crystallising. Reaching consumers through AI interfaces — rather than through traditional placements — is becoming a real media buy, not a thought experiment.

The playbook is still being written, but the directional decision is already live: marketers must now decide how much budget to allocate to AI-mediated impressions versus conventional display, search, and social. Brands that wait for the channel to mature risk ceding early-mover authority in AI environments.
ev: MarTech Series · Jellyfish Share of Model

themes.head: AI Is Restructuring Marketing Teams Internally
body: AI is not simply automating tasks — it is redrawing org charts. Reports on how agencies are evolving, how marketing teams are being reshaped from the inside, and why the future belongs to marketers who make colleagues smarter all converge on a single point: the unit of value is shifting from individual execution to AI-amplified judgment.

Klaviyo's acquisition of an agency team & its technology is a concrete example: capability is now bought as human-plus-model bundles. Leaders who treat AI as a tool for the same old headcount structure will fall behind those who redesign roles around AI leverage.
ev: MarTech · marketers who make others smarter
MarTech Series · Klaviyo acquires agency tech

themes.head: Governing AI Cost & Trust Infrastructure
body: Three distinct infrastructure launches this month — CloudZero's financial control plane for AI, DXC & Primary's AI-native Zero Trust platform, and Kyndryl's agentic modernization services — reveal that enterprises are moving past "will AI work?" to "how do we control what it costs and whether it can be trusted?" Cost observability and security are becoming table-stakes layers beneath every AI deployment.

For marketing technologists this is a strategic decision point: budget for governance tooling now or face runaway inference costs and security exposure later. The vendors who win the next cycle will be those who bundle capability with accountability, not just performance metrics.
ev: Agile Brand · CloudZero financial control plane
MarTech Series · DXC Zero Trust AI platform

themes.head: Customers Reward AI That Serves Them, Not You
body: YouGov brand-leadership data and Coca-Cola FEMSA's CX consistency story both reinforce what MarTech stated plainly: customers do not reject AI — they reject AI deployed for the brand's convenience at the expense of their own. The distinction is deciding whether AI is used to cut costs internally or to genuinely improve the experience on the customer's terms.

Observe.AI's recognition in conversational IVR & the guidance on giving AI the right context both point toward the same operational requirement: AI interactions need human-grade empathy signals and accurate situational awareness to feel helpful rather than evasive. Brands that get this right build loyalty; those that don't accelerate churn.
ev: Agile Brand · YouGov AI brand leadership
MarTech · how to give AI context

month.takeaway: Across every layer — ad formats, org structures, infrastructure, and CX — AI is forcing marketers to make explicit choices they used to defer: who you're targeting (humans or agents), how you govern cost and trust, and whether your AI deployment serves customers or merely your own margins.
